purpose: Reusable, source-verified player-specific sequences for Philadelphia Gamecast. This batch distinguishes a verified celebration from an iconic signature football move and does not invent named signatures.

productionContract.camera: three-quarter Gamecast hero angle; preserve the approved Dallas camera and avoid camera jumps
productionContract.lighting: shared neutral stadium key/fill/rim rig; identical approved Dallas production lighting
productionContract.anchor: bottom-center ground-contact anchor; any intentional airborne motion must resolve to the same projected world anchor
productionContract.scale: reuse locked player-specific PHI base-chibi proportions; no sequence rescaling
productionContract.appearance: reuse locked current official Philadelphia Eagles headshot appearance and skin tone; never infer appearance from name
productionContract.uniform: Philadelphia current uniform geometry and current roster number remain locked across every frame

sourceAuthority.note: Philadelphia's official highlight explicitly describes Smith capping his sack of Lamar Jackson with a dice-roll celebration. The asset name stays descriptive to that verified footage and does not claim a broader nickname or unsupported ritual.

animation.rootMotion: minimal; rise from sack finish and perform the compact dice-roll gesture over the same bottom-center world anchor

beats.direction: transition from the existing sack finish into a balanced upright defender stance without foot teleporting
bring both hands together naturally near the torso as if gathering dice; elbows remain compact and silhouette readable
brief controlled two-hand shake gesture with shoulders relaxed; preserve face visibility and current player proportions
hands move down and slightly forward in a concise rolling release; no exaggerated floor travel or invented flourish
brief downward glance/settle that sells the dice-roll concept while feet remain planted near the anchor
return cleanly to reusable post-play defender stance

sourceAuthority.note: The Eagles officially describe the backwards/reverse hurdle and later call it iconic while documenting its ESPY Best Play win. It is intentionally classified as a signature football move, not mislabeled as a celebration.

animation.rootMotion: event-driven airborne arc supplied by Gamecast locomotion; chibi animation controls body orientation and hurdle pose while landing resolves to the projected run-path foot anchor

beats.direction: enter from existing run-after-catch/run locomotion with ball secured and player-specific proportions locked
plant and lift into the recognizable backwards hurdle entry; keep motion athletic and grounded in the verified play rather than cartoon exaggeration
hips rise over the obstacle plane as torso rotates/back-leans through the iconic airborne silhouette; maintain secure ball control
bring legs back toward landing alignment while preserving the backwards-hurdle read and avoiding limb intersections
absorb landing with bent knees at the projected run-path anchor; no scale pop or foot slide
blend immediately back into reusable run-after-catch locomotion

rules: Current 2026 player identity and number must remain consistent with the PHI roster snapshot and official current player page.
A celebration is only named when official or otherwise authoritative evidence supports the gesture.
An iconic football move may be encoded as a signature sequence for Gamecast but must not be mislabeled as a celebration.
Appearance remains governed by locked current official headshot references from the earlier PHI appearance phase.

requirements: Sequence entry and exit blend with PHI action-pose keys without camera, scale, lighting, or anchor pops.
Uniform number, face, skin tone, hair/facial-hair reference and body proportions remain unchanged through every beat.
Transparent alpha edges remain clean during fast hand, leg and airborne motion.
Signature event tags never replace generic fallback celebrations/actions for players without verified signatures.
